cse-2014-2-cs-33.approach: For a cyclic access pattern larger than memory, OPT evicts the page just used (it will be needed furthest in the future) — exactly what MRU does. LRU/FIFO evict the page needed soonest and fault on every access.

steps.title: First pass
steps.body: Pages 101–120 are never used again. Pages 1–20 fault and replace them (all policies alike). From page 21 on, every policy must evict one of the resident pages from the current pass.

steps.title: What OPT evicts
steps.body: Next pass needs pages in order 1, 2, 3, …; among the resident pages, the one used furthest ahead is the most recently used one. So OPT evicts the most recently used page — MRU makes the same choice at every step and hence the same number of faults.

steps.title: LRU/FIFO/LIFO
steps.body: LRU and FIFO always evict the page that is needed soonest in the loop, so all $3\times100=300$ accesses fault. LIFO evicts the last page loaded: after the first fault, pages 101–119 stay resident forever and a single frame rotates through 1–100, so it also faults on all 300 accesses. MRU (= OPT here) keeps 19 useful pages and faults far less.

optionAnalysis.reason: LRU evicts the page needed soonest in a loop larger than memory: 300 faults, far more than OPT.
FIFO behaves like LRU on this pattern: 300 faults.
LIFO strands the dead pages 101–119 and rotates one frame: 300 faults.
Correct: MRU evicts exactly the page OPT evicts.

pitfalls: Choosing LRU because it is the usual "good approximation" to OPT — it is the worst case for cyclic scans.
cse-2014-2-cs-33.verification: Traced the start of pass 2: resident {1..19, 100}; at page 20 OPT evicts 19 (needed furthest ahead), which is also the most recently used page, so MRU matches OPT step by step.
